FoodHub Data Analysis¶

Context¶

The number of restaurants in New York is growing rapidly, catering to the increasing demand from students and busy professionals who rely on food delivery due to their hectic lifestyles. Online food delivery services offer a convenient solution, providing access to a variety of restaurants with just a few taps on a smartphone.

FoodHub, a food aggregator platform, connects customers with multiple restaurants through a single mobile app. The app streamlines the food ordering and delivery process:

  1. Customers place an order through the app.
  2. The restaurant receives the order and confirms it.
  3. A delivery person is assigned to pick up the order once it is ready.
  4. The delivery person collects the food and delivers it to the customer's location.
  5. The customer receives the order and can provide a rating in the app.

FoodHub earns revenue by charging a fixed margin on each delivery order collected from partnered restaurants.

Objective¶

FoodHub maintains a database of customer orders, which contains valuable insights about restaurant demand and customer preferences. The company aims to analyze this data to enhance the overall customer experience and optimize business operations.

As a Data Scientist at FoodHub, the goal is to analyze the provided dataset and address key business questions posed by the Data Science team. The findings from this analysis will help the company make data-driven decisions to improve service efficiency and customer satisfaction.

Data Description¶

The dataset contains information about various food orders placed through the FoodHub platform. Below is a detailed description of the dataset:

Data Dictionary¶

Feature Description
order_id Unique identifier for each order
customer_id ID of the customer who placed the order
restaurant_name Name of the restaurant from which the order was placed
cuisine_type Type of cuisine ordered by the customer
cost Total cost of the order
day_of_the_week Indicates whether the order was placed on a weekday (Monday–Friday) or weekend (Saturday–Sunday)
rating Customer rating for the order (out of 5)
food_preparation_time Time (in minutes) taken by the restaurant to prepare the order (calculated from order confirmation to pick-up)
delivery_time Time (in minutes) taken by the delivery person to deliver the order (calculated from pick-up to drop-off)

Top 5 Restaurants by Order Volume¶

The dataset is analyzed to identify the top 5 restaurants that have received the highest number of orders. This provides insights into customer preferences and helps in understanding which restaurants are the most popular on the platform.

In [362]:
# Groups the data by 'restaurant_name', counts the number of orders ('order_id') for each restaurant, 
# sorts them in descending order, and selects the top 5 restaurants with the most orders.
df.groupby(['restaurant_name'])['order_id'].count().sort_values(ascending=False).head(5).index
Out[362]:
Index(['Shake Shack', 'The Meatball Shop', 'Blue Ribbon Sushi',
       'Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken', 'Parm'],
      dtype='object', name='restaurant_name')

So, the five top restaurant in terms of the number of orders are: "Shake Shack", "The Meatball Shop", "Blue Ribbon Sushi", "Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken", and "Parm".

The dataset is analyzed to determine which cuisine type is ordered the most on weekends. Identifying popular weekend cuisines helps in understanding customer preferences and can assist in optimizing restaurant offerings and promotions.

Identifying Restaurants Eligible for Promotional Offers¶

To enhance restaurant visibility, the company plans to provide a promotional offer in advertisements. Restaurants must meet the following criteria to qualify:

  • Have received more than 50 ratings
  • Maintain an average rating greater than 4

The dataset is analyzed to identify the restaurants that fulfill these conditions and are eligible for the promotional offer.

In [382]:
# Filter the data to exclude rows where the rating is 'Not given'
filtered_df = df[df['rating'] != 'Not given']
# Convert the 'rating' column to integers
filtered_df['rating']= filtered_df['rating'].astype(int)
# Group the data by 'restaurant_name' and calculate the mean and count of ratings for each restaurant
grouped = filtered_df.groupby('restaurant_name')['rating'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
# Filter restaurants where the average rating is greater than 4 and the count of ratings is greater than 50
grouped[(grouped['mean']>4) & (grouped['count']>50)]
Out[382]:
mean count
restaurant_name
Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken 4.328125 64
Blue Ribbon Sushi 4.219178 73
Shake Shack 4.278195 133
The Meatball Shop 4.511905 84

The restaurants with rating count of more than 50 and the average rating greater than 4 are: Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken, Blue Ribbon Sushi, Shake Shack, and The Meatball Shop

Calculating Net Revenue Generated by the Company¶

The company applies a tiered commission structure based on order cost:

  • 25% commission on orders costing more than $20
  • 15% commission on orders costing more than $5

The dataset is analyzed to compute the total revenue generated from all orders based on this commission structure.

In [383]:
# Find the minimum value in the 'cost_of_the_order' column
df['cost_of_the_order'].min()
Out[383]:
4.47
In [384]:
# Calculate the net revenue based on the cost of the order
df['net_revenue'] = df['cost_of_the_order'].apply(lambda x: x*0.25 if x>20 else (x*0.15 if x>5 else 0))
In [385]:
# Calculate the total net revenue
df['net_revenue'].sum()
Out[385]:
6166.303

The net revenue generated by the company across all orders is 6166.303.

Analyzing Total Delivery Time¶

The company aims to assess the total time required for food delivery, which includes both preparation time and delivery time.

To evaluate efficiency, the dataset is analyzed to determine the percentage of orders that take more than 60 minutes from the time the order is placed until it is delivered to the customer.

In [386]:
# Create a new column 'total_time' that is the sum of 'food_preparation_time' and 'delivery_time'
df['total_time'] = df['food_preparation_time'] + df['delivery_time']
In [387]:
# Calculate the proportion of orders with a total time greater than 60 minutes
df.loc[df['total_time']>60]['order_id'].count() / df.shape[0]
Out[387]:
0.1053740779768177

10.54 of orders take more than 60 minutes to get delivered from the time the order is placed

The dataset is analyzed to determine if there are any significant variations in delivery times based on the day of the week.

Conclusion and Recommendations¶

Conclusions and Business Recommendations¶

Based on the analysis, key insights are derived to understand customer preferences, order trends, and operational efficiency.

Conclusions:¶

  • American cuisine is the most popular among all.
  • Orders are significantly higher on weekends than on weekdays.
  • A large portion of the ratings column consists of "Not given" values.
  • Delivery times are longer during weekdays.
  • The ratings start at 3, with no 1 or 2 values present in the ratings column.

Recommendations:¶

  • Address Missing Ratings: Since there are no ratings of 1 or 2 and many entries are marked as "Not given," investigate whether dissatisfied customers are opting not to provide ratings. Consider replacing numerical ratings with simpler feedback options, such as a thumbs-up or thumbs-down system, to encourage participation.

  • Increase Weekday Orders: Explore why orders are lower on weekdays. Could this be due to a lack of convenience for people ordering while at work? Simplifying the ordering process or offering promotions during weekdays could help balance the order volume and drive more sales.

  • Focus on Cuisine-Specific Strategies: While there are more restaurants offering American cuisine, Japanese restaurants have a higher number of orders per restaurant. Similarly, while Italian restaurants rank third in total orders, Chinese restaurants have a higher order count per establishment. This suggests the potential for increasing the number of restaurants offering Japanese cuisine or diversifying the restaurant options to improve the overall success of the app.
